summary.headline: Both orders and revenue behind target, and the quarter stands at 85.5% of target with nine weeks left.

points.what: Orders reached 90.0% of the weekly target and revenue 91.3%, despite orders rising 9.9% week on week.
points.so_what: Order growth was not enough to close the week's gap to target.

points.what: Orders came in at 745, outside the 8-week range, against an 8-week average of 689.
points.so_what: This is an unusually high order week rather than a continuation of the recent pace.

points.what: Revenue slipped 0.7% week on week to $50,652 while orders rose, and AOV fell 3.7% to $81.70.
points.so_what: More orders at smaller baskets explains why revenue did not follow the order increase.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 5.4 pp to 16.8%, a notable move, and is above last year's 16.2%.
points.so_what: With each percentage point of cancellations worth $609, this rise is holding back revenue against target.

points.what: QTD revenue is $201,573 against a target to date of $235,861, leaving a gap of $34,288 with 9 weeks left in the quarter.
points.so_what: Reaching the full-quarter target of $774,555 requires $572,982 in the remaining weeks, far above the recent weekly pace.

points.what: The cancellation rate at 16.8% is the highest in the 8-week history and is rated bad both week on week and year on year.
points.so_what: Cancellations are eroding revenue at $609 per percentage point, a risk to watch if the level persists.

points.what: Orders grew 58.5% and revenue 58.6% year on year, below the 75% growth the targets assume.
points.so_what: Growth at this rate keeps the gap to target widening rather than closing.

points.what: The week finished behind on both measures: orders at 90.0% of target, a gap of 83 orders, and revenue at 91.3%, a gap of $4,808.
points.so_what: The week added to the shortfall rather than recovering any of it.

points.what: YTD revenue attainment is 85.5%, behind target, against a full-year target of $3,888,802.
points.so_what: The year is starting from a deficit that later weeks would have to absorb.

points.what: Hitting the full-year target requires $75,250 a week for the remaining 49 weeks, against a current 8-week run-rate of $50,757.
points.so_what: The required pace sits far above what the business is currently delivering, so the full-year target is out of reach at this pace.

points.what: Search contributed 38 of the 67 additional orders, 56.7% of the week's order change, on 519 orders.
points.so_what: The week's order increase rests mainly on one source, so movements in Search set the direction of total orders.

points.what: North America was the largest regional contributor, adding 20 orders, 29.9% of the change, and grew 72.0% year on year.
points.so_what: It is the region closest to the 75% growth the targets assume.

points.what: APAC, the largest region at 43.1% of orders, added 12 orders and grew 3.9% week on week.
points.so_what: The biggest region grew slowest, which limits how far the total can move.

points.what: AOV fell 3.7% week on week to $81.70, a notable move outside its 8-week range, and is 0.8% above last year.
points.so_what: Order growth is not translating into revenue growth at the same rate.

points.what: The cancellation rate rose 5.4 pp to 16.8%, after 11.4% the previous week.
points.so_what: One percentage point of cancellations is worth $609, so this move is material to the revenue gap.

points.what: The 14-Day Return Rate for the mature week of 05 Jan 2026 was flat at 11.2%, above last year's 10.5%.
points.so_what: Return behaviour is unchanged week to week but sits worse than a year ago.

points.what: New signups rose 6.0% to 247 and 20.5% year on year, against order growth of 9.9% and 58.5%.
points.so_what: Orders are growing faster than signups, so the order increase is not matched by account growth.

anomaly flag acknowledged in the summary
sentences at most 30 words and 4 numbers
